A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same study, with 21 readable pages including Appendices A–G. Text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Distracting Control Suite experiments measuring latent-action quality and downstream performance, with ablations, generalization tests and additional appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the main experiments and the additional evaluations in Appendix F.

M1.justification: LAOM and LAOM+supervision retain identical architectures, objectives and training procedures. The components described in Sections 4–5, Figure 2 and Appendix D are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate cheetah-run, walker-run, hopper-hop and humanoid-walk with the same distractor and distractor-free datasets, novel-background tests and cross-embodiment scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: the main evaluations retain LAPO, IDM and BC, while the cross-embodiment comparisons retain LAPO and BC alongside the LAOM variants.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and Appendices C, E and G retain the same datasets, preprocessing, model settings, training budgets and evaluation procedures, including 2–128 labeled trajectories and 25 evaluation episodes.

E4.justification: The quantization and component ablations, latent-dimensionality analysis, novel-distractor generalization tests, cross-embodiment experiments and representation reconstructions are unchanged in Figures 4–10 and 13.

E5.justification: Both report averaging experiments over three random seeds and display identical uncertainty bands. No repeated-run information or statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative findings are unchanged, including the reported 0.44 normalized return for LAOM+supervision and Appendix F results. The changed figure reference does not change a result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, latent-action formulation and loss expressions remain identical. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about LAPO's difficulties with distractors, LAOM's improvements and the importance of action supervision. The main title is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of quantization, latent-action minimality and supervision remain unchanged. Appendix A retains the same limitations concerning real-world transfer, action-label availability and hyperparameter tuning.

D1.justification: Appendices C–E and G retain identical implementation details, hardware, precision, training times and hyperparameters. Both still promise release of code, configurations and logs after review.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix B and the reference list are unchanged, including positioning relative to LAPO, DynaMo and inverse-dynamics approaches. No cited works are added or removed.

P1.justification: The author spelling changes from Andrey Polubarov to Andrei Polubarov. Running headers replace 'Latent Action Learning in the Presence of Exogenous Noise' with the existing full title. The version stamp and one cross-reference change; prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption corrects its pointer to per-environment plots from Figure 1 to Figure 7. Apart from this caption edit and changed header text, figures, tables and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes Figure 1's misleading self-reference, correctly directing readers to the per-environment results in Figure 7, and aligns running headers with the title. These provide a small improvement in navigation and editorial consistency; scientific evidence, explanations and reproducibility remain unchanged.
